$comment: PERMISSION RULES FOR THIS PROJECT, so Daniel stops clicking 'Always'.
CLAUDE.md's 'Working without prompts' section measured the cause on
2026-11-15: 1,944 allow entries in the user-level settings, 87% of them
exact one-off strings with no wildcard, each captured by an 'Always' click
on a command that can never occur again. Adding more of those does not
help, because A COMPOUND COMMAND CANNOT MATCH ANY RULE.
These rules only cover the half that IS matchable. The other half is
habit, and it is the larger one: the shell already starts in this repo,
so every `cd ~/crumar-seven-editor && npm test` turns a rule-matchable
simple command into a compound one that nothing can ever allow. Same for
`npm test 2>&1 | tail -8` — the pipe makes it a different command.
Run them bare. Read the output.
DELIBERATELY NOT HERE: node, python3, npx, or any shell. A wildcard on an
interpreter is a blank cheque for arbitrary code. A script worth running
often gets a name in scripts/ or package.json and that name gets a rule.
Nothing that writes to the instrument or the library is here either.
